note: Adapted from the original English description by Harris (1966), the alate part of which quotes the original description by Sjöstedt (1926) (marked with quotation marks in the original); measurements are translated verbatim from the original, in millimetres. The original does not describe the worker.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Compared with A. guineensis the major soldier has the posterior margin of the head rounded, the anterior lobe of the pronotum not rounded-obtuse, and the marginal tooth of the left mandible smaller; the head is broadly rectangular, the sides and posterior margin curved; the mandibular apex is strongly incurved, the left mandible has 1 small tooth at the middle, and the edge below the tooth is straight as far as the small notch before the large basal process; the right mandible has no median tooth but bears a basal tooth. The alate is closely related to A. latinotus, differing in the slightly different build, the darker colour, the cross-veins in the subcostal area of the wing (absent in latinotus) and the ocelli markedly closer to the compound eye. Sjöstedt described the minor soldier as "closest to cavithorax, but with the mandibles more strongly incurved".

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: (Quoted from the original description of Sjöstedt 1926) Closely related to A. latinotus, differing in the slightly different build, the darker colour, and the cross-veins in the subcostal area of the wing, which A. latinotus lacks; the ocelli are closer to the compound eye than in A. latinotus. Head oval, dark brown with pale yellow; clypeus rather large; compound eyes nearly circular; ocelli oval, the ratio of long to short diameter 8:5, the distance from ocellus to compound eye equal to 1/4 of the ocellus long diameter; antennae 17-segmented; anterior margin of the pronotum with a deep median notch, posterior margin slightly concave; subcostal area of the wing with oblique cross-veins. Measurements (mm; 3 type specimens from Iri, Upper Uelé, Congo): head width (including the compound eyes) 1.86; compound eye diameter 0.54; ocellus long diameter 0.25, short diameter 0.15—0.18; ocellus to compound eye 0.06—0.08; pronotum width 1.64—1.72, length 1.00—1.09; hind tibia length 1.86—1.96; forewing length 20; forewing width 4.6.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: head orange-yellow, mandibles dark brown, antennae pale yellow; pronotum, abdomen and legs pale yellow, with many pale yellow setae. Head broadly rectangular, the sides and posterior margin curved; labrum short and wide, blunt at the tip; mandibular apex strongly incurved, the left mandible with 1 small tooth at the middle, the edge below the tooth straight as far as the small notch before the large basal process; right mandible without a median tooth, with a basal tooth; antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 small, segments 4 and 5 about equal and shorter than segment 2; postmentum wide, the sides slightly curved, strongly convex in cross-section. Pronotum with the anterior lobe small and pointed, the posterior margin concave. Minor soldier: head yellow, mandibles brown, antennae pale yellow; pronotum, abdomen and legs pale yellow, with inconspicuous short pale setae. Head oval; labrum large, blunt at the tip; mandibles slender, slightly incurved at the apex, the inner margin smooth; antennae 14—15-segmented. Anterior lobe of the pronotum not as pointed as in the major soldier, the posterior margin straight. Measurements (mm; table of the original, ranges only): head length including mandibles, major soldier 1.82—1.90, minor soldier 1.36—1.41; head length 1.23—1.32, 0.77—0.82; head width 1.11—1.18, 0.77; left mandible length 0.77—0.86, 0.68; pronotum width 0.73—0.86, 0.59; hind tibia length 1.04—1.09, 0.82—0.86.
